notes: Per-page performance budgets for the dashboard. Two independent rules judge every metric: an absolute ceiling (what acceptable means) and a band around the route's own baseline (what got worse). Only page_bytes is baselined. It is exact rather than near-deterministic here, and it is a property of the build alone: the dashboard is a static export, so a navigation returns a prebuilt page from the binary and every subresource is a content-hashed file beside it, while run data arrives over the API after load. Two pages carry the recharts chunks and are heavy for that reason; the rest differ by a few kilobytes of route code. Every number was measured over the wire against a served listener with the encoding the server offers a browser, which is what a page-weight budget means; the same pages unencoded measure 732,498 to 1,475,205 bytes and every one of them breaches the ceiling. The timings are unmeasured: this repository has no browser sweep of its own, and numbers taken on a machine running parallel gates would bake that in. Any tool reading this file must check version and refuse one it does not implement: unknown keys decode to zero, so a reader meeting a newer schema sees routes with no baselines, which is indistinguishable from routes nobody has baselined.

corpora.local: The dashboard as `sparkwing serve` serves it from a freshly created SPARKWING_HOME, measured with `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br`. page_bytes is the navigation response plus every subresource the page references, so it does not move with the runs in the store; it moves with the bundle `bin/build-web.sh` produces. It is the only corpus sparkwing has for this metric.

routes.note: The embedded documentation pages, server-rendered by internal/docsweb with inline styles and no subresources. This baseline is the unencoded size: the docs handler writes its own response and sits outside the encoding path the bundle and the app shell use. At 7 percent of the ceiling it has no budget problem, so the gap is recorded rather than closed.
